Get involved

There is a way for everyone to help.

Adopt, volunteer, foster or give. Pick what fits your life and we will show you where to start.

Find your cat at the café

Our adoptable cats live free-roaming in the café, so you can get to know their personalities before you decide.

  • Browse adoptable cats online, then meet them in person

  • Seniors can ask about our Pawsitively Seniors Program

Every helper starts here

Volunteering is the first step for everyone, including future fosters. Apply, come to an orientation, then pick the shifts that suit you.

  • Cat Care Crew, café assistant and desk attendant roles
  • Shifts run 9 AM to 6:30 PM, seven days a week
  • Volunteers must be 16 or older

How adoption works

We don't offer pre-adoptions. Every adoption starts with a visit to the café.

  1. Visit the café and meet the catsBook a session or walk in when there is space.
  2. Submit an adoption applicationA hold deposit can be placed after you meet your cat and apply. Holds last three café business days.
  3. Complete an in-person interviewApproval can take up to 24 hours.
  4. Sign the adoption contractThen it's time to take your new friend home.

Book a session to meet them

Every cat goes home

  • Spayed or neutered
  • Rabies and FVRCP vaccines
  • Microchipped
  • Dewormed
  • Tested and treated for fecal parasites
  • FIV and FeLV tested

What to bring

  • Valid photo IDApplicants must be 21 or older.
  • Landlord approvalOr a pet lease addendum, if you rent. Plus consent from anyone you live with.
  • A pet carrierNo carrier? We have cardboard carriers, and soft and hard carriers to buy.

Home / Shelter-to-Home Initiative

Saving 500 cats in one year

A collaboration between PALNV and Best Friends Animal Society to save surrendered, abandoned, sick and injured cats and kittens from Las Vegas’ municipal shelter, The Animal Foundation.

500cats transferred from the shelter in one year
August 2026July 2027

With a grant from Best Friends, we take cats from the shelter’s transfer list into foster homes and the café, where they get medical care, socialization and adoption support.

Who we take in

Cats land on the transfer list for three reasons. We say yes to all of them.

Medical needsIllness or injury the shelter can’t treat in time.
BehaviorScared or stressed cats who need a calmer place to settle.
No more roomCats who have to leave because the shelter is simply too full.

Cats we’ve saved so far

A few of the faces behind the 500.

Boots

Intake: July 29, 2026

Our very first Shelter-to-Home kitty. He has grown big and strong in foster care and will be ready for adoption very soon.

Olivia and her babies

Intake: July 29, 2026

Olivia was surrendered with her newborn kittens. She has calmed down a lot in foster care and is becoming a very sweet girl.

Cheese

Intake: August 5, 2026

Cheese was on the transfer list because of ongoing stomach troubles. Now he is getting the care he needs.

Mack

Intake: August 5, 2026

Mack was underweight and unwell when he came to us. He is putting on weight in foster care.

Ping and Pong

Shelter-to-Home

This brother and sister came in with eye and tummy infections. Now they are healthy and growing bigger every day.

Dwight, Michael, Toby, Stanley and Jim

Intake: August 15, 2026

Five brothers who arrived with ringworm and tummy troubles. We are doing everything we can to get them healthy.

Help us reach 500

The grant does not cover everything. Food, litter, bedding, toys and medical care all depend on you.

Volunteer with PALNV

The cats appreciate everyone who takes time out of their day to care for them. Every volunteer, and every future foster, starts here.

How to get started

  1. Apply onlineFill out a short volunteer application. Volunteers must be 16 or older.
  2. Attend a volunteer orientationHeld four times a month. Pick the one that suits you.
  3. Choose your shiftsShifts run between 9 AM and 6:30 PM, Monday to Sunday.
Sunday mornings1st and 3rd Sunday, 11:00 AM
Tuesday evenings2nd and 4th Tuesday, 5:30 PM
Apply to volunteer

Questions? Email volunteer@palnv.org or call 702-629-6351.

Ways to help

Cat Care Crew

Keep the cats’ living spaces clean and serve their meals each morning. Needed seven days a week.

Café assistant and desk attendant

Greet café visitors, answer the phone and help sessions run smoothly.

Ready to foster?

Once you are a registered volunteer, you can open your home to a cat in need.

Learn about fostering

Home / Foster

Foster a cat in need

Fostering is a short-term commitment that gives cats time to heal, grow and get ready for their forever home. You provide the love and care. We provide everything else.

What fosters need

  • Be 21 or olderAnd able to offer a safe, stable, loving home.
  • Register as a volunteer firstEvery foster starts in our volunteer program. Start here.
  • Apply and attend orientationComplete the foster application and the foster and volunteer orientation.
  • Agree to a home visitSo we can match the right cat to your home.

What to expect

Most foster placements last two weeks to two months. Our foster coordinator will match you with a cat that fits your lifestyle and schedule.

No special skills needed, just time, patience and dedication. Some cats are recovering from illness or injury, some are learning indoor life, and some are kittens who just need time to grow.

Apply to foster

Our programs

How PALNV helps cats, the people who love them, and the rescuers who work tirelessly for them.

Shelter-to-Home Initiative

Our biggest program this year. Saving 500 cats and kittens from the Las Vegas municipal shelter with Best Friends Animal Society.

See the initiative

Pawsitively Seniors Program

A long-term foster partnership placing adult and senior cats with qualifying seniors aged 65 and over. PALNV provides food, supplies and all medical care. Supported by the Gene Haas Foundation.

Food, supplies and medical care for 501(c)(3) rescues, known colony feeders and TNR trappers caring for community animals.

Home / About us

33 years of saving lives

Our mission is to save the lives of domestic cats and kittens living on our streets, through rescue, care and adoption.

Our story

  • 1993PALNV is founded by a small group worried about unwanted and abandoned animals.
  • 1994Granted nonprofit status.
  • 1994 to 2011More than 15,000 animals helped through spay and neuter, vaccinations, microchipping and adoption.
  • 2014PALNV moves its nonprofit operations to Las Vegas and focuses on community and shelter cats.
  • TodayRescued Treasures Cat Café, the Shelter-to-Home Initiative and the new PALNV Clinic.

What we work toward

  • Reduce cat overpopulation through spay and neuter
  • Improve the welfare of cats in our community
  • Give rescues the resources to keep saving lives
  • Promote responsible cat care through education
  • Build a safe haven for cats in need
